prompt: Which description of steroids matches the section?

choices.text: Molecules derived from the triterpenoid lanosterol, with a tetracyclic ring system
Molecules derived from arachidonic acid, with a five-membered ring
choices.why: That describes prostaglandins (Section 27.4).

choices.text: Molecules derived from the tetraterpenoid β-carotene, with two six-membered rings
choices.why: Steroids come from lanosterol, a triterpenoid, and have four rings.

choices.text: Esters of phosphoric acid with a sphingosine backbone
choices.why: That describes sphingomyelins (Section 27.3).

explanation: Steroids are molecules derived from the triterpenoid lanosterol whose structures are based on a tetracyclic ring system. The four rings are designated A, B, C, and D, beginning at the lower left.

prompt: The steroid ring system has four rings, A, B, C, and D. How many of them are six-membered rings?
explanation: Rings A, B, and C are six-membered rings that adopt chair conformations; ring D is the fourth, five-membered ring.

prompt: How do the six-membered rings of a steroid differ from a simple cyclohexane?

choices.text: They adopt chair conformations but can't undergo the usual ring-flips because of their rigid geometry
They are flat because the four rings are fused together
choices.why: Rings A, B, and C still adopt chair conformations.

choices.text: They adopt boat conformations because the ring fusions prevent chairs
choices.why: The section says the six-membered rings adopt chair conformations.

choices.text: They ring-flip faster than cyclohexane because the fusions add strain
choices.why: They don't ring-flip at all; their rigid geometry prevents it.

explanation: The three 6-membered rings (A, B, and C) adopt chair conformations but are prevented by their rigid geometry from undergoing the usual cyclohexane ring-flips.

prompt: Two cyclohexane rings are fused to give cis-decalin. What does cis mean here?

choices.text: Both groups at the ring-junction positions are on the same side of the two rings
The groups at the ring-junction positions are on opposite sides of the two rings
choices.why: That describes trans-decalin.

choices.text: Both rings are in boat conformations
choices.why: Cis and trans refer to the angular groups at the ring junction, not the ring conformations.

choices.text: The two rings share only one carbon atom
choices.why: In decalin the rings share two carbons, the ring-junction positions; cis refers to how the angular groups at those positions are placed.

explanation: With cis fusion to give cis-decalin, both groups at the ring-junction positions (the angular groups) are on the same side of the two rings. With trans fusion to give trans-decalin, they are on opposite sides.

prompt: Which statement correctly describes the ring fusions in steroids?

choices.text: The A–B fusion can be cis or trans, but the B–C and C–D fusions are usually trans
All three ring fusions are always cis
choices.why: The B–C and C–D fusions are usually trans, and the A–B fusion can be either.

choices.text: The A–B fusion is always trans, but the B–C and C–D fusions can be cis or trans
choices.why: This reverses the section: A–B is the fusion that can be either cis or trans.

choices.text: The C–D fusion can be cis or trans, but the A–B and B–C fusions are always trans
choices.why: It's the A–B fusion, not C–D, that can be either cis or trans.

explanation: As shown in Figure 27.6.1, steroids can have either a cis or a trans fusion of the A and B rings, but the other ring fusions (B–C and C–D) are usually trans.

prompt: What orientation does the hydroxyl group of cholesterol have, and why?

choices.text: Equatorial, which is generally more favorable than axial for steric reasons
Axial, which is generally more favorable than equatorial for steric reasons
choices.why: As with simple cyclohexanes, equatorial substitution is generally more favorable.

choices.text: It flips between axial and equatorial as the ring flips
choices.why: Steroid rings can't ring-flip, so each substituent is fixed as axial or equatorial.

choices.text: Axial, because the steroid rings are locked in boat conformations
choices.why: The rings are chairs, and cholesterol's –OH has the more stable equatorial orientation.

explanation: Substituents on the steroid ring system can be axial or equatorial. As with simple cyclohexanes, equatorial substitution is generally more favorable for steric reasons, and the hydroxyl group of cholesterol has the more stable equatorial orientation.

prompt: Lithocholic acid, found in human bile, is an A–B cis steroid. In its chair-conformation drawing (Exercise 27.6.2), what is the orientation of the hydroxyl group on carbon 3?

choices.text: Equatorial
Axial
choices.why: The exercise's answer shows the hydroxyl group at carbon 3 equatorial.

choices.text: It has no fixed orientation because the A ring can flip
choices.why: Steroid rings can't ring-flip, so the –OH group is fixed; it is equatorial.

choices.text: It lies flat in the plane of an aromatic A ring
choices.why: Lithocholic acid's A ring is a chair, not an aromatic ring. Estrone and estradiol are the steroids with an aromatic A ring.

explanation: In Exercise 27.6.2's chair drawing of lithocholic acid, an A–B cis steroid, the hydroxyl group at carbon 3 is equatorial.

prompt: In humans, most steroids function as hormones. What is a hormone?

choices.text: A chemical messenger secreted by an endocrine gland and carried through the bloodstream to target tissues
A structural lipid that forms the bilayer of the cell membrane
choices.why: That describes phospholipids (Section 27.3).

choices.text: A lipid used for long-term energy storage
choices.why: That describes fats (Section 27.1).

choices.text: An enzyme that catalyzes steroid biosynthesis
choices.why: Hormones are messengers, not catalysts.

explanation: Hormones are chemical messengers that are secreted by endocrine glands and carried through the bloodstream to target tissues. The two main classes of steroid hormones are the sex hormones and the adrenocortical hormones.

prompt: Which two compounds are the most important male sex hormones, or androgens?

choices.text: Testosterone and androsterone
Estrone and estradiol
choices.why: These are the two most important female sex hormones, or estrogens.

choices.text: Aldosterone and hydrocortisone
choices.why: These are adrenocortical hormones, a mineralocorticoid and a glucocorticoid.

choices.text: Progesterone and norethindrone
choices.why: Progesterone is the most important progestin, and norethindrone is a synthetic progestin.

explanation: Testosterone and androsterone are the two most important androgens. They are synthesized in the testes from cholesterol and are responsible for male secondary sex characteristics and for promoting tissue and muscle growth.

prompt: Which structural feature do the estrogens estrone and estradiol share, according to the section?

choices.text: A benzene-like aromatic A ring
An acyclic, open-chain structure
choices.why: Estrogens are steroids, built on the four-ring system.

choices.text: A six-membered, oxygen-containing ring
choices.why: That is the ring of the thromboxanes (Section 27.4).

choices.text: An A–B cis ring fusion with an axial hydroxyl group
choices.why: The section's point about estrogens is that both have a benzene-like aromatic A ring.

explanation: Estrone and estradiol, the two most important estrogens, are synthesized in the ovaries from testosterone. Both have a benzene-like aromatic A ring.

prompt: What is the role of progestins such as progesterone?

choices.text: Preparing the uterus for implantation of a fertilized ovum during pregnancy
Regulating the cellular salt balance between Na+ and K+
choices.why: That is the role of mineralocorticoids such as aldosterone.

choices.text: Regulating glucose metabolism and controlling inflammation
choices.why: That is the role of glucocorticoids such as hydrocortisone.

choices.text: Developing male secondary sex characteristics during puberty
choices.why: That is the role of androgens such as testosterone.

explanation: A progestin is a sex hormone that is essential in preparing the uterus for implantation of a fertilized ovum during pregnancy. Progesterone is the most important progestin.

prompt: Hydrocortisone is a glucocorticoid. What do glucocorticoids do?

choices.text: Help regulate glucose metabolism and control inflammation
Control tissue swelling by regulating the Na+/K+ salt balance
choices.why: That is the role of mineralocorticoids, such as aldosterone.

choices.text: Regulate the menstrual cycle
choices.why: That is a role of the estrogens.

choices.text: Promote tissue and muscle growth
choices.why: That is a role of the androgens.

explanation: Adrenocortical steroids, secreted by the adrenal glands, are of two types. Mineralocorticoids such as aldosterone regulate the salt balance between Na+ and K+. Glucocorticoids such as hydrocortisone regulate glucose metabolism and control inflammation; glucocorticoid ointments bring down swelling from poison oak or poison ivy.

prompt: What do most birth control pills contain, according to the section?

choices.text: A synthetic estrogen, such as ethynylestradiol, and a synthetic progestin, such as norethindrone
A synthetic androgen, such as methandrostenolone, and a synthetic estrogen
choices.why: Methandrostenolone (Dianabol) is an anabolic steroid, not a contraceptive component.

choices.text: A glucocorticoid, such as hydrocortisone, and a mineralocorticoid, such as aldosterone
choices.why: These are natural adrenocortical hormones, not oral contraceptives.

choices.text: Natural testosterone and natural progesterone
choices.why: The section describes the pills as mixtures of a synthetic estrogen and a synthetic progestin.

explanation: Most birth control pills are a mixture of two compounds, a synthetic estrogen such as ethynylestradiol and a synthetic progestin such as norethindrone.

prompt: What are anabolic steroids such as methandrostenolone (Dianabol)?

choices.text: Synthetic androgens that mimic the tissue-building effects of testosterone
Synthetic estrogens used in oral contraceptives
choices.why: Ethynylestradiol is the synthetic estrogen in birth control pills. Anabolic steroids are synthetic androgens.

choices.text: Natural glucocorticoids secreted by the adrenal glands
choices.why: Anabolic steroids are made in pharmaceutical laboratories and mimic testosterone, an androgen.

choices.text: Synthetic progestins that prepare the uterus for pregnancy
choices.why: Norethindrone is the synthetic progestin named in the section. Anabolic steroids are synthetic androgens.

explanation: Anabolic steroids, such as methandrostenolone (Dianabol), are synthetic androgens that mimic the tissue-building effects of natural testosterone.
